relevance_note: Single case report of a man with familial LCAT deficiency: "A homozygous mutation in the LCAT gene (c.355G>C, p.Gly119Arg) was identified."; both parents are heterozygous carriers.
method_note: Built by hand-written Python from my reading of the paper (no table transcription by script). In-scope people: the proband ('patient', rule 5; the paper calls him 'the proband' once), his two parents (tested heterozygous carriers; sex not stated, so 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2'), and his sister (described in relation to him with individual-level facts but untested and reportedly healthy; included as a described relative, scope arguable). Parents were described only as 'asymptomatic carriers'; no phenotypic_features rows were made for them because 'asymptomatic' names no specific feature. Sister: 'no history of ... renal disease, or visual disturbances' was not used to exclude narrower checklist items (CKD, nephrotic syndrome, proteinuria, corneal opacity); only anemia is excluded. Patient inheritance recorded as 'inherited unspecified parent' because both parents carry the variant (homozygous, biparental) and the enum has no biparental value. In silico predictions (PolyPhen-2, SIFT, CADD) are not recorded as functional evidence; LCAT enzyme activity was not measured. Pathogenicity for the parents' variant rows left 'not reported' (the in silico sentence is about the variant in general / the proband). Co-inherited HBA --SEA deletion (alpha0-thalassemia trait) recorded as a second-gene variant for the patient; zygosity not stated in words; variant type mapped from 'deletion' (listed among large fragment deletions in Table 2) to 'large deletion/CNV'. Lipid values: LDL (1.69, 0.87 mmol/L) and triglycerides (1.73, 0.72 mmol/L) are reported as values but not characterized as low/high by the authors, so those checklist items are 'not reported'; serum albumin 26.2 g/L likewise not recorded as a separate feature. 'No gross hematuria' does not exclude checklist 'hematuria' (narrow vs broad). Checklist 'lipoprotein x' marked observed from the authors' statement that renal biopsy revealed extensive Lp-X deposition (tissue, not plasma Lp-X). 'Glomerular foam cells' marked observed from 'foamy endothelial cells' in the glomerular capillary loops. CKD marked observed from treatment sentence 'slow the progression of chronic kidney disease' plus impaired renal function. Normal autoantibodies/immunoglobulins/light chains/anti-PLA2R and negative Coombs/PNH recorded as excluded abnormalities per D-27. Supplementary file (figure legends and tables) duplicates the main text; used for some severity details. No internal contradictions found. Note the paper reports transferrin saturation as '0.21%' (likely a unit issue; recorded as printed).
